verdict_reason: The estimator computes exactly its documented BLME formulation -- per-token relative Gaussian perturbation of the input embeddings, clean and perturbed forward passes, d_l = E_t||h_l - h'_l||, and log(d_l/d_0) with a least-squares slope in normalized depth -- and I verified the two claimed defects independently. (1) The bf16 resolution claim REPRODUCES: on gpt2 with an identical corpus, seed and noise draw the realized relative displacement at rel_eps=1e-3 is 1.0000e-03 (100.0%) in fp32, 8.4987e-04 (85.0%) in bf16 and 1.0179e-03 (101.8%) in fp16, against bf16's machine eps of 7.812e-03; at the new rel_eps=1e-2 it is 1.0000e-02 / 1.0120e-02 / 1.0002e-02, i.e. 100.0% / 101.2% / 100.0%, and at 5e-2 all three land within 0.1%. So the raise from 1e-3 to 1e-2 does what it claims about perturbation SIZE. (2) The hook leak is FIXED ON BOTH EARLY-RETURN PATHS, verified by counting layers[-1]._forward_hooks around a live call: 0 before, 0 after the 'No usable samples' return, 0 after the 'Degenerate divergence profile' return. Neither of those changes any computed value, so nothing here bears on fidelity.
comparable_reason: Two independent measurements say no. (a) STORAGE DTYPE. Same gpt2 weights, same 30 samples, same seed, same realized perturbation (0.01000 / 0.01012 / 0.01000): growth_log_ratio = 2.7956 (fp32), 4.6152 (bf16), 3.0699 (fp16) -- a 65.1% spread produced by the checkpoint's dtype alone. It is a rounding-noise floor, and I traced its scale dependence: the same spread is 18.2% at rel_eps=5e-2 (2.7975 / 3.3070 / 2.8167) and 7.1% at 1e-1 (2.8019 / 3.0003 / 2.8080), while fp32 is essentially eps-invariant across all three (2.7956 / 2.7975 / 2.8019). So the rel_eps raise fixed the perturbation size but did NOT fix the metric, which at the new default still differs by 65% between a bf16 and an fp32 copy of the same model. The study loads with dtype='auto', so Llama/Gemma/Qwen/SmolLM2 checkpoints are bf16 and GPT-2/Pythia are fp32. (b) DEPTH. Over 13 models growth_log_ratio has spearman +0.566 with n_layers (log-log fit L^+0.255) and growth_slope -0.478 with d_model.
github_reason: No code was released with either cited grounding. Li et al. 2025 (arXiv:2503.13530, quasi-Lyapunov analysis) publish no repository, and the Fernando & Guitchounts residual-stream line (arXiv:2502.12131) releases nothing that computes this quantity. The module is explicit that it is a clean-room BLME formulation citing that grounding, which is the honest framing. I did verify the module's own analytic anchor by construction: for a linear stack h_{l+1} = a h_l the divergence grows by |a| per layer, so growth_log_ratio = (L-1) ln|a| and growth_rate_per_block = ln|a| exactly -- and that is what the code computes.
paper_reason: Li et al. 2025 report a quasi-Lyapunov exponent qualitatively (regime labels and a chaoticity argument), not a reproducible per-model number on a stated corpus, and their setup is prompt-space perturbation on reasoning traces rather than embedding-space perturbation on a fixed corpus. There is no published figure this task should reproduce. A legitimate NONE.
confounds_reason: Measured over 13 models (distilgpt2, gpt2, gpt2-medium/large, pythia-70m/160m/410m/1b, opt-125m, SmolLM2-135M/360M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama-3.2-1B) at rel_eps=0.01. growth_log_ratio: spearman +0.566 with n_layers (p ~ 0.044), fits L^+0.255 -- it accumulates over every block traversed, so a deeper model scores higher for being deeper. growth_rate_per_block, the normalized twin, OVERCORRECTS: spearman -0.722 with n_layers (p ~ 0.005), log-log fit L^-0.745 with pearson -0.8552 -- a STRONGER depth association than the raw column, with the sign flipped, because growth_log_ratio grows only as L^0.255 while the divisor grows as L^1. Neither form is depth-free. Separately, initial_divergence carries spearman -0.863 with vocab_size (p ~ 0.0001) -- it is rel_eps times the mean embedding row norm, and is emitted unprefixed and feature-eligible.
defects: THE HOOK LEAK IS NOT FULLY FIXED: there is no try/finally, so an exception raised anywhere inside the sampling loop leaves the forward hook attached to layers[-1] for the rest of the process. Measured by counting layers[-1]._forward_hooks around a live call with the forward patched to raise on the third invocation: 0 before, 1 after. The two early returns are covered; an OOM, a tokenizer failure or any model-side raise is not -- and core.py catches per-task exceptions and continues to the next task, so the leaked hook survives into every later task in the run and pins the last activation tensor alive. The sibling dynamics/coe.py already wraps the identical hook in try/finally; this file does not.

THE dtype FIX DID NOT FIX THE METRIC. Same gpt2 weights at the new rel_eps=1e-2: growth_log_ratio 2.7956 (fp32) / 4.6152 (bf16) / 3.0699 (fp16), a 65.1% spread with the realized perturbation identical to 1.2%. The `_meta_realized_rel_eps` guard checks the perturbation size and passes (101.2%), so it does NOT catch this. It is the larger of the two dtype problems and it is undisclosed.

growth_rate_per_block, the depth-normalized twin, is a WORSE depth proxy than the column it normalizes: spearman -0.722 vs +0.566 with n_layers over 13 models, log-log L^-0.745 with pearson -0.855. Dividing by n_transitions assumes the log-divergence is proportional to depth; measured, it grows as L^0.255.

initial_divergence has spearman -0.863 with vocab_size over 13 models (range 0.0045-0.0338) and is feature-eligible and unprefixed. It is rel_eps times the mean embedding row norm, so it measures the embedding scale, not any dynamical property.

CONFIG: num_samples=10, and 10 sentences of <=128 tokens is a thin basis for a per-layer expectation. I did not find it to be the dominant error term (the dtype spread at n=30 is the same 65% as at n=10), but there is no uncertainty estimate emitted at all -- no std, no SEM, no per-sample spread.

The default fallback dataset (`Perturbation growth probe sentence {i}.`) is a set of near-identical short sentences; a run that reaches it produces a number on a degenerate corpus with nothing in the output to say so.
fix: Wrap the sampling loop in try/finally so `_hook.remove()` runs on the exception path too (verified leak: hooks 0 -> 1 after a raise inside the loop); dynamics/coe.py has the pattern. Compute the clean and perturbed forwards in fp32 (promote-and-restore, as repe_steering_effectiveness already does) or emit a _meta_ dtype flag and refuse cross-dtype comparison -- the same weights currently read 2.7956 vs 4.6152 in fp32 vs bf16 at the shipped rel_eps. Prefix initial_divergence with _meta_ (rho -0.863 with vocab_size). Either drop growth_rate_per_block or replace it with a residual against the fitted L^0.255 trend, since as shipped it is a stronger depth proxy than the raw column. Emit a per-sample std or SEM.
